slot.brief: Ask for the number and location of tetrahedral and octahedral voids in an fcc unit cell, possibly counting how many lattice atoms enclose a given void type.

stem: Which description correctly gives the numbers, locations and surrounding atoms of the two types of voids in an fcc unit cell?
options: 8 tetrahedral voids at the centres of the eight smaller cubes, each surrounded by 4 atoms; 1 octahedral void at the body centre only, surrounded by 6 atoms.
8 tetrahedral voids at the centres of the eight smaller cubes, each surrounded by 6 atoms; 4 octahedral voids at the body centre and edge centres, each surrounded by 4 atoms.
8 tetrahedral voids at the centres of the eight smaller cubes, each surrounded by 4 atoms; 4 octahedral voids at the body centre and edge centres, each surrounded by 6 atoms.
8 tetrahedral voids at the centres of the eight smaller cubes, each surrounded by 4 atoms; 13 octahedral voids at the body centre and all twelve edge centres, each surrounded by 6 atoms.

verdicts.working: An fcc unit cell has 8 tetrahedral voids at the centres of its eight smaller cubes, each with coordination number 4. Its octahedral voids comprise 1 body-centre site and 12 edge-centre sites shared among 4 cells, giving 1 + 12/4 = 4 per unit cell; each has coordination number 6.

working:
Tetrahedral voids: $8$ at the centres of the eight smaller cubes; each has $4$ surrounding atoms.
Octahedral voids: $1$ body-centre site + $12$ edge-centre sites, each shared by $4$ cells, gives $1 + 12/4 = 4$ per unit cell.
Each octahedral void is surrounded by $6$ atoms.

Independent check: An fcc unit cell has 8 tetrahedral voids at the centres of its eight smaller cubes, each with coordination number 4. Its octahedral voids comprise 1 body-centre site and 12 edge-centre sites shared among 4 cells, giving 1 + 12/4 = 4 per unit cell; each has coordination number 6.
solution: Tetrahedral voids lie at the centres of the eight smaller cubes, each surrounded by 4 atoms. Octahedral voids: $1+\frac{12}{4}=4$ per unit cell, at the body centre and edge centres; each is surrounded by 6 atoms.
